title: Depression hardship and rationing
summary: Checking garbage cans before school, stamps for goods, and his song 'Hard Times In '29'.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: The Depression years and the WPA band

blocks.x: And times were very hard, like, back during the Depression. We used to have to go and check out all the garbage cans before we'd go to school, to see if there was anything good in there worth using, like shoes or a shirt -- anything that you might be able to use, a pot or a pan or anything. Because during that early period... It was really, really rough during the early Depression. And I remember all those things that had written on them "not to be sold," you know, the powdered milk and the flour and the sugar and shoes... You had stamps for everything, you know, and one person a month could get shoes in the family. All these things, you know.
In fact, I've got a thing that I wrote called "Hard Times In '29" that I'm going to get somebody to record one of these days, you know... But I remember all of these things that went down.
